I will do it mostly the way that has kept my land steady, and I will only change a little. I have 16.9 mu, and I cannot risk the whole year on fancy ideas. I will keep most of the land in wheat-maize because that is the safe backbone here, and I have well water, so I can push grain a bit without being afraid of dry weather. I will leave only a small piece for chili and cotton, because those bring cash, but they also eat labor and money. I watch what people around me do. If the neighbors use a better wheat seed or a hybrid maize and I saw it fill the ear well, I will use that too. On fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than watch the crop turn yellow and lose yield. Wheat I will feed a little heavier because good wheat stand matters from the start. Maize I will also feed well after wheat comes off, because if I starve summer maize, the ears get small fast. Chili needs steady water and more sprays because bugs and disease come often, so I will not plant too much. Cotton I will keep on a small area, manage it clean, and not overspend on it if the price does not look good. For tillage, I will use machine rotary tillage on most land because it is fast for my size and saves my back. With 4 people in the house and 16.9 mu total, I can manage this plan without making the season too tight.
